title: Associations of vitamin status and T-lymphocyte subsets with tic severity in children: a cross-sectional study using the Yale Global Tic Severity Scale
date_caveat: Indexing is not publication; PubMed history timezone unverified.
design: Single-center cross-sectional, treatment-naive children under 14; n=41. Median symptom duration one month.
outcome: YGTSS global 0–100, total tic plus impairment, not total tic score alone.

negative_evidence.interpretation: Vitamin associations do not survive primary multiplicity correction; subgroup pattern is nonmonotonic.

limits: Small selected pediatric sample, residual confounding, influential observations, no longitudinal direction, no immune mechanism or supplementation efficacy. Not persistent severe adult evidence.
access: Primary abstract and selected published methods/aggregate results inspected; no participant rows, figures, supplements or source body saved.
correction_retraction_check: No linked notice in official metadata. Correction-query hit reflects statistical correction wording, not a correction notice.
authors: Fengming Zhu; Yun Gao; Zhenlong Zhang; Shumin Kang; Weidong Xu; Jian Zhang
adverse_events: No intervention tested; adverse-event evidence not extracted.
funding_conflicts: Not extracted in this bounded pass.
attrition: Complete-data cross-sectional selection; source-population exclusions and missingness not quantitatively audited.
cohort_overlap: Related-cohort overlap not established; do not count as independent replication.
claim_not_supported: Supplementation efficacy, clinical benefit, immune causation, diagnostic biomarker or adult treatment target.
